newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition threatens to block tax reform.
newsitem.headline: German opposition threatens to block tax reform.

text.p: The German lower house opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Friday they will use their majority in the upper house of parliament to block the government's tax reform unless there is a broad tax cut.
"Either we agree on a clear tax cut for 1998 or you can forget it," SPD party boss Oskar Lafonataine told parliament.
German opposition threatens to block tax reform

Because the SPD governs a majority of the 16 federal states, it holds sway in the upper house of parliament, which can block some legislation passed by the lower house, where Chancellor Helmut Kohl's centre-right coalition holds power.
Kohl's tax reform calls for huge tax cuts in 1999.

The SPD, instead of opposing the tax reform outright as many conservative politicians had expected, has instead criticised the lack of relief for the middle class and demanded the tax cuts in 1998, ahead of the next general election.
